newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos is hopeful that the talks resumed by the government and the National Democratic Front will be sustained until a final peace agreement is forged in June. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Malaysian investors would cut their investments in the Philippines after the Philippine Supreme Court blocked the sale of the historic Manila Hotel to a Malaysian consortium. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Senators on Sunday lambasted President Ramos for using the Supreme Court's decision on the Manila Hotel privatisation case as an excuse to justify the move to amend the Constitution. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Delays in the privatisation of certain assets and the failure of some government-owned and -controlled corporations to remit dividends were among the major concerns raised during the initial stage of the two-week consultation between the Philippines and the International Monetary Fund team. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Central Bank is inclined to allow commercial banks to grant loan guarantees which would pave the way for the effective increase in the single borrower's limit on banks. (TIMES/JOURNAL)
- The Monetary Board has approved the rules and regulations covering the flotation of Europeso bonds by financial institutions in the international capital markets. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
